lens: The tape went quiet midweek — the S&P barely moved — but the deal calendar stayed busy: Procter & Gamble agreed to buy Thorne for $3.8B, ContextLogic struck an $850M specialty-chemicals deal, and cross-border divestitures signed across energy (Gran Tierra), software (Command Alkon) and media (Clear Channel’s Spain business), several with two covered banks apiece and two fresh Deutsche Bank mandates.

stories.headline: Perella Weinberg advises Thorne on its $3.8B sale to Procter & Gamble
stories.why_it_matters: L Catterton agreed to sell Thorne — a science-backed health-and-wellness (vitamins, minerals, supplements) leader — to Procter & Gamble (NYSE: PG) for $3.8B in cash, expected to close in Q4 2026. The release names Perella Weinberg Partners (with Canaccord Genuity) as financial adviser to Thorne (sell-side); no adviser was named for P&G. A sponsor-to-strategic sale of a consumer-health brand runs brand, regulatory, and QofE diligence toward close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Perella Weinberg (Thorne) — a $3.8B consumer-health sale to a strategic runs brand, regulatory and quality-of-earnings diligence a secure room organizes through close.

deal_clock.event: L Catterton agrees to sell Thorne to P&G ($3.8B)

stories.headline: BofA (lead) and RBC advise Gran Tierra on its $1.33B sale of its Colombia/Ecuador business to Maurel & Prom
stories.why_it_matters: Gran Tierra Energy (NYSE/TSX: GTE) agreed to sell its Colombia and Ecuador business — all of its South American assets — to Maurel & Prom (a Pertamina subsidiary) for $1.33B total consideration (~$315M net cash proceeds), repositioning the company for fully financed growth. The release names BofA Securities as lead financial adviser (and fairness-opinion provider) to Gran Tierra, with RBC Capital Markets also advising (sell-side). A cross-border upstream divestiture runs reserve, regulatory and confirmatory diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage BofA and RBC (Gran Tierra) — a $1.33B cross-border upstream divestiture runs reserve, regulatory and confirmatory diligence a data room supports.

deal_clock.event: Gran Tierra agrees to sell Colombia/Ecuador business ($1.33B)

stories.headline: Morgan Stanley advises gChem and Piper Sandler advises ContextLogic on the $850M specialty-chemicals acquisition
stories.why_it_matters: ContextLogic (Nasdaq: LOGC) agreed to acquire gChem — a specialty-chemicals maker (DMSO for pharma, semiconductors, ag and aerospace), sold by EagleTree Capital — for $850M enterprise value. The release names Morgan Stanley as exclusive financial adviser to gChem (sell-side) and Piper Sandler as financial adviser to ContextLogic (buy-side). A sponsor-exit chemicals carve-out runs environmental, contract and QofE diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Morgan Stanley (gChem) and Piper Sandler (ContextLogic) — an $850M specialty-chemicals sale runs environmental and quality-of-earnings diligence a secure room keeps organized.

stories.headline: Deutsche Bank advises Francisco Partners and Evercore advises Thoma Bravo on the sale of software maker Command Alkon
stories.why_it_matters: Francisco Partners agreed to acquire Command Alkon — a construction and heavy-building-materials software provider — from Thoma Bravo (terms undisclosed), expected to close in H2 2026 subject to regulatory approval. The release names Deutsche Bank Securities as financial adviser to Francisco Partners (buy-side) and Evercore as financial adviser to Thoma Bravo / Command Alkon (sell-side). A sponsor-to-sponsor software buyout runs code, contract and QofE diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Deutsche Bank (Francisco Partners) and Evercore (Thoma Bravo) — a sponsor-to-sponsor software buyout runs code-escrow, contract and QofE diligence a secure room organizes.

deal_clock.event: Francisco Partners agrees to acquire Command Alkon from Thoma Bravo

stories.headline: Moelis and Deutsche Bank advise Clear Channel Outdoor on the ~$132M sale of its Spain business to Atresmedia
stories.why_it_matters: Clear Channel Outdoor (NYSE: CCO) completed the sale of its Spain out-of-home advertising business to Atresmedia for ~€115M (~US$132M), continuing its international-market divestiture program. The release names Moelis & Company and Deutsche Bank Securities as financial advisers to Clear Channel (sell-side). A cross-border media carve-out runs local-regulatory and separation diligence through close.
stories.suggested_action: Note Moelis and Deutsche Bank (Clear Channel) — a cross-border media carve-out runs local-regulatory and TSA/separation diligence a data room supports.

deal_clock.event: Clear Channel completes sale of Spain business to Atresmedia (~$132M)

stories.headline: Lazard and JPMorgan advise Ascensus; Raymond James advises AmericanTCS on the completed retirement-platform acquisition
stories.why_it_matters: Ascensus completed its acquisition of AmericanTCS — a retirement, trust-and-custody and fintech provider (terms undisclosed) — expanding its platform and capabilities. The release names Lazard and J.P. Morgan as financial advisers to Ascensus (buy-side) and Raymond James as financial adviser to AmericanTCS (sell-side). A financial-services platform acquisition runs client-contract, regulatory and integration diligence.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Lazard/JPMorgan (Ascensus) and Raymond James (AmericanTCS) — a retirement-platform combination runs client-contract and regulatory diligence a secure room organizes through integration.

stories.headline: Markets pause after the August run — S&P flat, Dow +0.85%, Nasdaq -0.04% — with the 10Y steady at ~4.63%
stories.why_it_matters: US equities took a breather midweek: S&P 500 roughly flat (~7,744), Dow +0.85% (~54,547), Nasdaq slightly negative (-0.04%, ~26,574), with the VIX easing to ~16.3 and the 10Y Treasury steady at ~4.63%. Advisory names held their recent gains — Goldman +1.7%, Jefferies +1.6%, JPMorgan +0.7% — as a steady stream of mid-cap and cross-border deals kept signing. A calm tape and full deal calendar keep signed processes moving on schedule.
stories.suggested_action: Use the steady tape and continued signings to keep the conversation on execution — clients want live processes on schedule; room readiness protects the timeline.

talking_point.quote: The tape went quiet midweek but the deal calendar didn’t: P&G paid $3.8B for Thorne, ContextLogic struck an $850M chemicals deal, and cross-border divestitures signed across energy and media — several with two covered banks apiece. A calm market is when signed processes need to stay on schedule, and that’s a room-readiness conversation. How are you thinking about execution on the mandates you’re carrying this week?
talking_point.use_with: Consumer, energy, industrials, software and financial-institutions coverage teams (esp. Perella Weinberg, BofA, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank, Moelis)
talking_point.context: Pairs a flat market with a steady, cross-sector signing day — a natural way to open an execution-certainty conversation.

pipeline_watch.note: Named covered-bank mandates and sector heat. Rumored / no-adviser situations live in the Rumor Mill.

skeptics_corner.note: Unconfirmed leads — rumored deals and situations with no adviser named yet (or advisers unconfirmed). Real reporting, but treat as speculative: chase them, don’t quote them on a call.

items.lead: Bending Spoons agreed to acquire enterprise-software maker Airtable for a reported ~$1.285B enterprise value (~$2.25B equity incl. cash), all-cash, announced Aug 4. Airtable is private.
items.why_unverified: Deal is real (Business Wire, Aug 4) but the primary release was unreachable and no aggregator snippet named a financial adviser — no covered-bank involvement confirmed either way.

items.lead: DBGI disclosed an unsolicited $77.58/share all-cash acquisition proposal (Aug 5) and said its board "recently retained a financial adviser" to evaluate it — but the adviser is not named.
items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed that an adviser was retained, but no name disclosed and the proposal is unsolicited/early — chase-early edge, not a confirmed mandate.

items.company: GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) — Patient Care Solutions
items.lead: On its Q2 call, CEO Peter Arduini confirmed a formal review of strategic options for the Patient Care Solutions segment, explicitly including “a sale and other value-enhancing transactions.” Segment Q2 revenue was $675M, down 13.3%.
items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed that a review is underway — but whether it sells, at what price, to whom, with which adviser, and on what timeline are all unconfirmed. A potential carve-out mandate, not a rumored deal.
